findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 3 projects, synced last week." followed by a list containing only "Data Warehouse Cutover" and "Mobile App Revamp"
findings.fix: Either add the third project to the list (or a visible indicator like "showing 2 of 3" with a way to see the rest) or correct the count in the paragraph to match the list.

findings.evidence: "Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on."
findings.fix: Either remove this promo copy or link it to an actual reporting section/page and show invite progress toward the goal.
findings.violation: This references an "advanced reporting add-on" feature that does not exist anywhere else in the document, and the invite flow only supports inviting one person at a time with no progress indicator toward the "3 teammates" goal.

findings.evidence: `<form>` has no `action` attribute, and `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` has no associated navigation
findings.fix: Give each form an action/handler consistent with the rest of the prototype's hash-based navigation (e.g., route Save to a confirmation state or back to the relevant hub).
findings.violation: Unlike every other flow transition in the mockup (which uses `<a href="#...">` links), this Save button (and the equivalent Save buttons in #invite-member-save-btn and #notification-settings-save-btn) has no defined destination, so submitting the form goes nowhere.

findings.fix: Add label text (e.g., "Duplicate project") inside the button or via `aria-label`.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text or accessible label, so users (and screen readers) cannot tell what it does.

findings.evidence: form with `#invite-member-save-btn` (type="submit") alongside a separate `Continue`
findings.fix: Collapse this into one action - either make Save itself route to #invite-sent, or remove the redundant Continue link.
findings.violation: There are two different controls that appear to complete the same invite action (Save vs. Continue), but only Continue actually navigates anywhere; this is confusing and inconsistent with other single-action forms like project-settings.
